# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 22 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 22 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_022_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 4, Chapter 1

**1** The fourth vision which I saw, brothers and sisters, came twenty days after the previous one — a foreshadowing of the tribulation that is coming. **2** I was walking on the country road, about ten stades from the main road, through terrain that is difficult of access. **3** As I walked alone I was asking the Lord to complete the revelations and visions he had shown me through his holy church, to strengthen me and grant repentance to his servants who had stumbled, so that his great and glorious name might be glorified — for he had thought me worthy to show me his wonders. **4** While I was glorifying and thanking him, something like a responsive voice came to me: "Do not be double-minded, Hermas." I reasoned within myself, "How can I be double-minded, after being established by the Lord and having seen such glorious things?" **5** Walking a little further, brothers and sisters, I saw dust rising up as if toward the heavens, and I said to myself, "Are cattle coming?" — but it was only about a stade away. **6** As the dust rose higher and higher I suspected something supernatural. A little sunlight broke through, and I saw a great beast like an enormous sea-monster, from whose mouth fiery locusts were issuing. The beast was about a hundred feet in length, and its head was like an earthenware vessel. **7** I began to weep and beg the Lord to rescue me from it. Then I recalled the word I had heard: "Do not be double-minded, Hermas." **8** So, brothers and sisters — clothed in faith in the Lord and calling to mind the great and glorious things he had taught me — I took courage and faced the beast. It was charging with such rush and force that it could have destroyed an entire city. **9** When I drew near, the great beast stretched out on the ground and did nothing but extend its tongue; it lay completely still until I had passed it. **10** The beast had four colors on its head: black; then fiery and blood-red; then golden yellow; then white.

---

### Council Notes

Vision 4 is the dramatic and artistic peak of the Visions. Structurally it recapitulates ch. 4 (where the same beast encounter was briefly described), now as the full Vision 4 narrative.

The encounter follows a precise psychological sequence: (1) divine warning "do not be double-minded," (2) Hermas's initial self-assurance, (3) the appearance of the terrifying beast, (4) collapse into weeping and prayer, (5) recollection of the word, (6) recovery of faith, (7) courageous advance, (8) the beast's submission.

This sequence models the dynamic of faith under eschatological pressure — not that the faithful feel no fear, but that they recall the word and act in faith regardless.

The four colors (v. 10) will be interpreted in ch. 23 as the four stages of the tribulation-and-salvation cycle.
